messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable retro pixel turn-based strategy game set during the Battle of Stalingrad, with playable Soviet and German factions.

## Requirements
- Build the game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- For any screenshot checks, save a small JPEG (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest image.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone browser game in one `index.html` file, with an original title, “Ashes of Stalingrad.”
- Assumed an objective-control victory condition: first side to 20 points wins; players command rifle squads, tanks, and artillery.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a responsive, pixel-art-style tactical game interface with a faction-selection briefing, battlefield canvas, unit readout, objectives, score display, and field dispatch log.
- Added turn-based movement, firing, terrain cover and movement costs, strategic-point scoring, enemy AI turns, and win/defeat screens.
- Added Soviet and German playable sides and a new-operation/replay flow.

### Active
- Validate JavaScript syntax and test gameplay in a browser; no browser test or screenshot has been completed.

### Blocked
- The attempted syntax check failed because it searched for a `<script>` tag using a regex that did not match; it returned `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '1')`. This did not validate the current file.

## Next Move
1. Run a syntax check against the script contents in `index.html`.
2. Launch the game and test faction selection, movement, firing, enemy turns, objective scoring, and replay; capture a latest small JPEG if doing visual checks.
3. Fix any issues found and report assumptions briefly when finishing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: entire game implementation; currently uncommitted.

## Important Context
- `index.html` was replaced after an initial failed write left it containing only the latter portion of the game script; the current version includes complete HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- No changes have been committed.

playwright-cli screenshot [target]

screenshot of the current page or element

Arguments:
  [target]                    exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector
Options:
  --filename                  file name to save the screenshot to. defaults to `page-{timestamp}.{png|jpeg|webp}` if not specified.
  --type                      image format. if unset, inferred from the filename extension, otherwise png. (one of: png, jpeg, webp)
  --full-page                 when true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport.
  --hires                     when true, captures a high-resolution screenshot using device pixels (accounts for the device pixel ratio), instead of css pixels.
